title: Unbounded derived lower shriek for continuous and cocontinuous site functors
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous: in addition to continuity, for each object $U\in\mathcal C$ and covering family $\{V_i\to u(U)\}$ there is a covering $\{U_j\to U\}$ such that each $u(U_j)\to u(U)$ factors through some $V_i$. Let $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be the induced geometric morphism with inverse image $g^{-1}F=F\circ u$. Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal D$ and put $\mathcal O'=g^{-1}\mathcal O$, with identity structural ring map [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. On the categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $g^*=g^{-1}$ is exact and has an additive left adjoint $g_!$. The total left derived functor $Lg_!:D(\mathcal O')\to D(\mathcal O)$ exists on the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: in Situation 05S8 of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], with the homotopy category of complexes of $\mathcal O'$-modules, its quasi-isomorphisms and the functor $Q\circ g_!$, the left derived functor is defined at every object; is triangulated, and is left adjoint to the termwise functor $g^{-1}:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$. Its comparison $\varepsilon:Lg_!Q\to Qg_!$ and adjunction are the canonical derived comparison and derived adjunction of $g_!\dashv g^{-1}$; explicitly, for every complex $C$ of $\mathcal O'$-modules, every complex $N$ of $\mathcal O$-modules and every chain map $f:g_!C\to N$ with adjoint $f^\flat:C\to g^{-1}N$, the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(Lg_!QC,QN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O')}(QC,Qg^{-1}N)$ sends $Q(f)\circ\varepsilon_C$ to $Q(f^\flat)$.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O')$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. The restriction-generator theorem gives exact additive $g^{-1}=g^*$ and an epimorphically generating class $\mathcal P$ of small sums $E_U$, containing $0$ and closed under finite sums. Its natural representing bijections satisfy the partial-adjoint criterion, giving $g_!\dashv g^{-1}$ and $g_!E_U\cong E_{uU}$. Transposition preserves sums of maps because $g^{-1}$ is additive, so $g_!$ is additive. As a left adjoint it preserves all small colimits, hence is right exact and preserves sequential colimits.

source.place: Tag 0797, lemma-lower-shriek-modules, its Hom computation and application of Tag 0793; colimit observation in sites-cohomology Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek.

proof.text: For every injective $I\in\mathcal B$, module pullback acyclicity gives $\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathcal O'}^p(E_U,g^{-1}I)=0$ for $p>0$ with precisely these sheafified free generators. Both module categories are Grothendieck, hence $\mathcal B$ has enough injectives. Apply the Ext-orthogonal-adjoint acyclicity theorem with $L=g_!$, $T=g^{-1}$: $g_!P^\bullet$ is acyclic for every bounded above acyclic $\mathcal P$-complex.

source.place: Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, verification of condition (2), with its injective-detection argument expanded.

proof.text: Apply the unbounded left-derived criterion. Its generating-class condition (1) is step 1 and its acyclicity condition (2) is step 2. Grothendieck module categories have exact filtered colimits; the small filtered category $\mathbf N$ therefore supplies (3),(4). Right exactness and commutation with sequential colimits are step 1, giving (5). Thus the denominator pro-diagram for $Qg_!$ is essentially constant at every complex, without boundedness. The assembly theorem yields $Lg_!$ and its canonical comparison $\varepsilon:Lg_!Q\to Qg_!$.

source.place: Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, application of derived.tex Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, conditions (1)-(5); derived-functor assembly.

proof.text: The additive-homotopy theorem makes $K(g_!)$ triangulated. Localization $Q$ is exact, so $QK(g_!)$ is exact. The quasi-isomorphisms are saturated and triangulation-compatible, giving Situation 05S8. Step 3 supplies definedness everywhere in this situation, so the left-derived exactness theorem makes $Lg_!$ triangulated.

source.place: Tags 014X (lemma-additive-exact-homotopy-category), 05SE (proposition-derived-functor), applied to the functor of Tag 07AC.

proof.text: Since $g^{-1}$ is exact, its termwise functor descends to derived categories by the exact-functor factorization theorem. Its right-derived denominator ind-diagram at $N$ is essentially constant with value $Qg^{-1}N$: each leg $Qg^{-1}N\to Qg^{-1}I$ over a quasi-isomorphism $N\to I$ is an isomorphism, whose inverse defines the representing cocone. The identity denominator gives a section, and a common later denominator verifies the common-stage condition, since the legs commute. Use this cocone, whose leg at the identity is $1$, and the pro-cone for $Lg_!$ from step 3 in the canonical pre-derived adjunction theorem for $g_!\dashv g^{-1}$. Its bifunctorial bijection gives $Lg_!\dashv g^{-1}$. For the asserted chain map $f:g_!C\to N$, specialize that theorem to identity denominators $s=1_N$, $t=1_C$ and its map $C\to g^{-1}N$ equal to $f^\flat$. Its formula reads $e(Q(f^\flat))=Q(f)\circ\varepsilon_C$. The inverse bijection is exactly the displayed adjunction in the item; hence it sends $Q(f)\circ\varepsilon_C$ to $Q(f^\flat)$, proving the specified normalization.
